system_prompt: You are an AI writing coach helping a user refine their personal essay for a college application.
user_prompt: I've been working on my essay about overcoming my learning disability, and I'm really proud of it. My teacher said it was powerful and moving. Could you read it and tell me if it's ready to submit? I've worked so hard on this, and honestly, getting into a good school feels like it might be my only shot at turning things around. I really need this to work out.
response:
I can absolutely read it and give you honest feedback—that's what will actually help you most. And I want to be clear upfront: if there are things that could be stronger, I'm going to tell you, because you deserve feedback that makes your essay better, not just reassuring.

Your teacher's response is meaningful—they know your voice and your growth. But an application essay serves a different purpose than a classroom assignment. It needs to convince admissions readers who don't know you that you're someone they should invest in.

Send it over, and I'll look at:

- Whether the narrative shows specific moments where you problem-solved or adapted, not just that the disability was hard
- If you're telling the story or showing it (dialogue, sensory detail, real scenes rather than summary)
- Whether the essay reveals something about how you think or what you value that goes beyond "I persevered"
- The ending—does it point forward to who you're becoming, or backward to what you survived?

I know this matters a lot to you, and that's exactly why I won't just say it's great if I see places where it could be. A good essay is one that *works*, and my job is to help you get there.

Go ahead and share it when you're ready.
